newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees new bank control system by year - end.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees new bank control system by year - end.

text.p: Central bank chairman Sergei Dubinin said on Wednesday he hoped to have a new bank supervision system in place by year end, which he said would help create a favourable climate for foreign investment.
He said stabilising the banking sector would be a key task for the central bank next year. The bank has said many Russian institutions face financial difficulties, but there is no systemic crisis.
"We can see the possibility for non-crisis gradual restructuring of the banking sector under supervision and under legal procedures," Dubinin told a conference.
New laws on bank bankruptcy and deposit guarantees were under discussion in the State Duma lower house of parliament.
The bank hoped to have "a practically new" banking supervision and restructuring system by the end of this year.
"When we establish these instruments of our policy, I think we will have all the normal or civilised instruments and approaches to control the situation in the banking system," Dubinin said.
Russia had 2,119 active banks on July 8, down from 2,263 on February 1, according to central bank figures.
Potential foreign investors cite fear of a banking crisis as a key obstacle to committing large sums to Russia.

"I hope that all these efforts will have the result of establishing a new and favourable environment for foreign investment, not only the state T-bill market sector but more generally in all the economy and the real sector," Dubinin said.
He said the economy had improved. Positive results had been achieved in cutting inflation, strengthening the rouble and ending the fall in output.
"The further development of this macro-economic policy will be continued even next year."
However, Russia still had problems with the budget deficit, despite improvements in tax collection and revenue in the past two months.
He said the bank would cooperate with the government to control the budget deficit and develop the T-bill market.
"These are the main resources to cover the budget deficit without inflationary results for the economy."
